newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - WASHINGTON POST FRONT - AUG 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - WASHINGTON POST FRONT - AUG 11.

text.p: The Washington Post included the following stories on its front page on Aug. 11:
WASHINGTON - President Bill Clinton will exercise the line-item veto to strike at least two items from the tax and spending bills he signed last week, administration officials said.
WASHINGTON - AT a Fairfax, Virginia apartment complex, immigrants from 20 countries provide a potent mix.
WASHINGTON - For the first time in nearly a decade and a half as mayor of the District of Columbia, Marion Barry found his government turned over to the D.C. financial control board.
MEXICO CITY - A series of drug-related scandals have some people wondering if Mexico is turning into another Colombia.

BOGOTA, COLOMBIA - In a country notorious for having one of the world's highest homicide rates, Colombians and foreigners living here are turning to protective clothing to allay their sense of vulnerability.
WASHINGTON - Labor Secretary Alexis Herman warned United Parcel Service against hiring replacement workers and urged UPS and the Teamsters union to resume talks to end a strike that began Aug. 4.
